title: Hazardous or unidentified contaminants
audience: Trainees and workers on the pressure cleaning (all heights) track, and supervisors who decide whether a surface may be pressure cleaned. Mould content in this lesson is kept with full warnings. It is not authority to remove mould.
learningOutcomes: Identify surfaces and substances that must not be pressure cleaned until they are identified and assessed.
Explain why pressure cleaning can spread contamination, including mould spores, into air, water and other areas.
Apply stop, containment and referral decisions to a simulated job with unknown or hazardous contamination.

instruction.heading: Why contamination changes the job
instruction.body: A pressure cleaner moves a large volume of water at force. When the surface is contaminated, the jet can break up the contamination, throw it into the air as fine droplets or aerosol, and carry it into drains, soil and neighbouring areas. A job that looks like a routine clean may therefore spread a hazard, rather than remove it. The first decision on any surface is whether the contamination is known, ordinary and safe to clean with the approved method.

instruction.heading: Identify before you clean
instruction.body: Look at the surface and its surroundings before the equipment starts. Note any staining, odour, residue, powder, loose material, growth or damage that is not ordinary dirt. Ask the site controller about past spills, chemical storage, animal waste, flooding or repairs. Do not touch, scrape or test an unidentified substance by hand. If the material cannot be identified from the labels, safety data sheets or the site controller's records, treat it as unknown and do not pressure clean it.

instruction.heading: Mould and biological growth: full warning
instruction.body: Mould is a biological growth that can release spores. Pressure cleaning can spread those spores into the air and carry them, in water, into wall cavities, floor junctions, drains and other rooms, so it is not an appropriate routine method for mould. Do not pressure clean mould, and do not treat this lesson as authority to remove it. A worker who sees mould-like growth, a musty smell, or water damage behind a surface stops, keeps other people away from the area, records what was seen, and refers the job. Mould remediation requires its own assessment, containment, respiratory protection and waste controls, and those are covered in the High-risk cleaning module (family lesson HR04-mould-remediation).

instruction.heading: Asbestos and suspect materials
instruction.body: Older buildings may contain asbestos-containing materials in sheeting, flooring, fibre cement and other finishes. Pressure cleaning can break these materials and release fibres. The Queensland council page advises against using pressure cleaners on asbestos-contaminated materials (last modified 22 July 2025). If a surface may contain asbestos, do not pressure clean it, do not scrape or cut it, and stop the job. The Safe Work Australia model code on managing and controlling asbestos in workplaces is a model code whose legal effect depends on each jurisdiction (publication date blank). Refer the job to a competent person who can identify the material.

instruction.heading: Chemicals, SDS and wash water
instruction.body: Before using any cleaning product on an unknown surface, check the product's label and safety data sheet. Do not mix products, and do not use a product on a surface it is not designed for. In Queensland, a council page says pressure-cleaning wastewater is a regulated contaminant under the Environmental Protection Regulation 2014 (Schedule 10) and may not go into gutters or the stormwater system (last modified 22 July 2025). Collect, divert or refer the wash water as the job plan and the site rules require.

instruction.heading: Stop, contain and refer
instruction.body: Where the contamination is unknown, the response is stop, contain and refer. Stop the equipment, keep people and animals clear, close off the area where practical, and record the location and the appearance of the material. Refer the job to the site controller and to a competent person who can identify the substance or growth. Do not restart until the material is identified and a written method is approved. If a worker feels unwell after contact or exposure, stop work, move to fresh air, and seek medical advice.

instruction.heading: Licence and authority boundary
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, clearance, certificate or authority to remove mould, asbestos, hazardous chemicals or other restricted contamination. A pressure cleaning worker does not give a clearance statement for any surface that was contaminated.

procedure: Inspect the surface and surroundings for staining, odour, residue, growth, loose material or damage before starting.
Ask the site controller about past spills, chemical storage, flooding, repairs and any known contamination.
If the substance or growth cannot be identified, stop and do not pressure clean the surface.
For any mould-like growth or musty smell, stop, keep people clear and record what was seen.
For any material that may contain asbestos, stop, do not disturb it, and refer it to a competent person.
Check the label and safety data sheet of any approved product, and never mix products.
Keep wash water out of stormwater, and collect or divert it as the job plan requires.
Record the observations, the decision, the people told and the referral made.

workedExamples.situation: A customer asks for the rear wall of a house to be pressure cleaned. The wall has black growth in the lower corners and a musty smell at the base of the wall.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the wall be pressure cleaned, and what is the next step?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The growth may be mould, and pressure cleaning can spread spores and water into the wall. Stop, keep the area clear, and record the growth and the smell. Tell the customer that a pressure clean is not suitable for this surface until the growth is assessed. Refer the job to a competent person, and note that mould remediation sits in the High-risk cleaning module.

workedExamples.situation: A driveway has a pale, powdery residue that the customer says has been there for years. The building is old and the driveway edge has a cracked sheet material beside it.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must the worker do before any pressure cleaning?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop before the residue or the cracked sheet is disturbed. The material is unidentified, and the sheet may contain asbestos. Do not pressure clean the area. Keep people clear, record the location and appearance, and refer the job to a competent person who can identify the material before any method is approved.

equipmentAndPpe: Identification checklist for surface, staining, odour and growth
Product labels and safety data sheets for every approved product on site
Barriers or cones to keep people and animals clear of the area
Respiratory and skin protection as the job pack specifies for the substance, and eye protection

commonErrors.error: Pressure cleaning mould because the surface looks like dirt.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, record the growth and refer it. Mould remediation is outside a routine pressure clean.

commonErrors.error: Disturbing an old sheet material that may contain asbestos.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop before disturbing it and refer it to a competent person for identification.

commonErrors.error: Mixing products to strengthen the clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only the approved product, as its label and safety data sheet direct, and never mix products.

commonErrors.error: Letting contaminated wash water run into stormwater.
commonErrors.prevention: Collect or divert the wash water as the job plan requires.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Mould: pressure cleaning can spread spores and water into building materials. This lesson is not authority to remove mould, and mould remediation is covered in the High-risk cleaning module (family lesson HR04-mould-remediation). No mould regulatory position was checked in this pass.
Asbestos: the Safe Work Australia model code on managing and controlling asbestos in workplaces is a model code whose legal effect depends on each jurisdiction (publication date blank).
Stormwater and wastewater: the Queensland council page says pressure-cleaning wastewater is a regulated contaminant and may not go into gutters or the stormwater system (last modified 22 July 2025).
Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, clearance, certificate or authority to remove mould, asbestos or hazardous contamination.

qualityStandard: The surface is inspected and any unknown or hazardous contamination is recorded before the equipment starts.
Unidentified material is not pressure cleaned, and the job is stopped and referred.
No product is mixed, and wash water is kept out of stormwater.
No clearance or safety statement is given for a contaminated surface.
documentationEvidence: Pre-clean observation record with the location, appearance and odour of any contamination
Site controller answers on past spills, chemicals, flooding and repairs
Stop and referral record with the person notified and the decision owner
Product labels and safety data sheet references for any product used
summary: Unknown or hazardous contamination is a reason to stop and refer, not a reason to pressure clean.
Pressure cleaning can spread mould spores, asbestos fibres and contaminated water.
Mould remediation and asbestos handling are outside a routine pressure clean and are referred.
This lesson grants no clearance, licence or authority for restricted contamination work.

knowledgeChecks.question: A surface shows black growth and a musty smell. What is the correct first response?
options: Stop, keep people clear, record the growth and refer the job
Pressure clean it on a low setting to lift the growth
Treat it with a stronger product and continue the clean
Scrape it off by hand before the clean starts today

knowledgeChecks.question: Why can pressure cleaning be unsuitable for mould?
options: Mould is too weak to notice on most surfaces at all in the house
It can spread spores and water into the air and building materials
It always kills all mould on every surface it touches in the house
It only affects the surface colour of the material and the paint

knowledgeChecks.question: An old sheet material beside a driveway may contain asbestos. What must happen?
options: Clean it gently with a low-pressure setting on the jet
Pressure clean it quickly before others see it on the site
Stop, do not disturb it, and refer it to a competent person
Cut it back to make the clean easier to do on the day

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker wants to mix two products to clean a stubborn residue. What is the correct response?
options: Mix them in the bucket for a stronger clean on the surface today
Mix them if the customer agrees and signs a short form for the job
Mix them, then rinse with extra water to remove any traces left behind
Use only the approved product as its label and safety data sheet direct

knowledgeChecks.question: Does this lesson grant a clearance or licence to remove mould or asbestos?
options: No, it grants no clearance, licence or authority for restricted contamination work
Yes, for mould only, once the worker has been trained on the job and signed off by the owner
Yes, once the quiz is passed by the worker and the employer signs off for the job
Yes, if the site controller agrees to it in writing for the whole job today and signs

officialReferences.title: Safety data sheets
officialReferences.covers: Safe Work Australia fact sheet (dated April 2012) says an SDS is arranged under 16 headings, from Identification to Regulatory information and Any other relevant information. It says a register of hazardous chemicals must include the current SDS for each chemical listed, and that a supplier must provide a manufacturer's or importer's SDS free of charge on first supply or when asked. It refers manufacturer and importer duties to the Code of Practice. Publisher: Safe Work Australia.

officialReferences.title: Asbestos removal and handling requirements by state
officialReferences.covers: NSW only: a Class A licence is needed to remove any amount of friable asbestos; a Class B licence is needed to remove more than 10 m2 of non-friable asbestos; the licensed removalist must notify SafeWork NSW at least five calendar days before removing friable asbestos (any amount) or more than 10 m2 of non-friable asbestos. The page does not cover other states.
